details: Bitcoin spot Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) have experienced significant outflows, totaling approximately $4 billion over the past three weeks, with May alone registering $2.30 billion. This marks the largest negative performance since November 2025, reflecting a decline in short-term confidence among institutional investors and keeping the "Fear and Greed Index" in the "fear" zone. However, some analysts suggest that heavy outflows can act as a contrarian bullish indicator, potentially signaling a market bottom and anticipating a significant price movement following a period of compressed volatility.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See Billions in Outflows as Market Confidence Wanes

details: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has approved prediction-market operator Kalshi to launch a perpetual futures contract for Bitcoin in the U.S. In parallel, Coinbase received permission to enable its U.S.-based clients to access cryptocurrency options and perpetual futures trading on Deribit, an offshore derivatives exchange, directly through the Coinbase app. This development significantly expands regulated crypto derivatives offerings within the United States.
title: US Regulators Greenlight Crypto Perpetual Futures for Kalshi and Coinbase

details: The U.S. Treasury Department has confiscated approximately $1 billion in cryptocurrency tied to Iranian financial networks. This action underscores ongoing regulatory and enforcement efforts by global authorities to combat illicit financial activities and money laundering facilitated by digital assets.
title: US Treasury Seizes Nearly $1 Billion in Iran-Linked Crypto

details: A bipartisan bill, the "American Reserve Modernisation Act of 2026 (ARMA)," has been introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives. This legislation proposes establishing a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve by locking up the government's existing $26 billion in crypto holdings for a period of 20 years, with future acquisitions to be budget-neutral. The bill is currently in its preliminary stages.
title: US House Introduces Bill for Strategic Bitcoin Reserve

details: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has renewed his criticism of the proposed Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, expressing concerns that it could create an uneven regulatory landscape. He argues that the legislation might allow cryptocurrency firms to offer products akin to bank deposits without being subjected to equivalent safeguards and oversight.
title: Jamie Dimon Criticizes Proposed Digital Asset Market Clarity Act
